title: Resumable streaming consumer and event-dispatch pattern for Python SDK (chat completions)
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background:
Teams using the Python SDK for chat completions want a robust streaming consumer primitive that: resumes mid-response after transient network failures, exposes typed events (chunk/delta/end/error), and gives application authors easy hooks for backpressure and idempotent retries. Current patterns in repo are ad-hoc (async iterators, callback shims) and lead to duplicated logic in apps (resume tokens, assembling split tokens, distinguishing transient vs terminal errors).

Problem statement:
- Network blips and ephemeral 5xx responses cause poor UX for long responses (lost output, repeated tokens, or duplicated writes).
- Consumers need deterministic, testable semantics for resume and for retrying request submission (idempotency).
- Backpressure surface: developers need an API to signal the runtime to slow/flush based on application queue lengths.

Proposed solution (high level):
Introduce a ResumableStreamConsumer primitive in the Python SDK that: 
1) Normalizes server events into a small set: CHUNK, DELTA, CHECKPOINT, END, ERROR. CHECKPOINT events carry opaque resume tokens supplied by the server or synthesized client-side.
2) Provides an EventDispatcher to register fine-grained handlers (on_chunk, on_delta, on_checkpoint, on_error, on_end) while returning a composable async iterator for simple cases.
3) Implements a small resumability protocol: client sends idempotency_token + last_checkpoint to request; on reconnect, client rehydrates KV-cache of partial buffers and requests continuation.
4) Exposes backpressure signals: consumer.pause()/consumer.resume() or await consumer.wait_for_drain(threshold_ms) to let apps block reading when downstream is slow.

API sketch (pseudocode):
class ResumableStreamConsumer:
    def __init__(self, client, request, idempotency_token=None):
        ...
    async def start(self):
        """Start reading stream, return self as async iterator"""
    def on_chunk(self, handler: Callable[[str], None]): ...
    def on_checkpoint(self, handler: Callable[[str], None]): ...
    async def checkpoint(self) -> str: ...  # returns last checkpoint token
    async def resume(self, checkpoint_token: str): ...
    async def pause(self): ...
    async def resume_flow(self): ...

Simple usage (iterator):
async for ev in ResumableStreamConsumer(client, req):
    if ev.type == "CHUNK":
        write(ev.text)
    elif ev.type == "END":
        break

Advanced usage (event dispatcher):
consumer = ResumableStreamConsumer(client, req, idempotency_token=unique_id)
consumer.on_chunk(lambda c: write(c))
consumer.on_checkpoint(lambda token: store(token))
await consumer.start()

Retry semantics and idempotency:
- New SDK option `idempotency_token` is sent on initial create. Server will accept token and apply at-most-once semantics for request side-effects where available.
- Retries of the connection use exponential backoff (base=150ms, factor=2, max=3s) and jitter. Total attempts default to 5.
- On reconnect, SDK replays last checkpoint token to request continuation. If server cannot resume, it returns a START_OF_STREAM marker and the SDK falls back to a full re-run (but will deduplicate via idempotency_token when supported).

Backpressure and resource controls:
- Consumer exposes `set_buffer_limit(tokens=int)` and will apply backpressure to the internal read loop when buffer > limit.
- If the app does not drain in `max_pending_ms` (configurable, default 2000ms), SDK emits a WARNING-level event and can optionally drop oldest chunks (configurable policy: block | drop_oldest | pause_socket).

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover: checkpoint token lifecycle, resume behavior when server supports resume, fallback path when server rejects resume token.
- Integration test against the local mock streaming server simulating: mid-stream disconnects, duplicate-delivery, split token boundaries.
- Performance: reconnect+resume end-to-end time < 500ms median under normal network (10ms RTT), 99th percentile < 2s.
- Correctness: application-visible duplication rate <= 0.1% on simulated reconnects.
- SDK docs: example in quickstart + long-form guide on resume semantics and migration notes.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement ResumableStreamConsumer in feature branch and tests.
2) Add lightweight mock server harness in /tests/streaming/mock_server.py to replay patterns.
3) Ship behind feature flag `PY_SDK_RESUMABLE_STREAM` and enable for internal beta customers.
4) Collect telemetry (resume_success, resume_failure_reason, reconnect_latency) and dashboard in Console (linked to org-internal dashboard).
5) Gradual enablement: internal devs -> select customers -> default on for 1.9.0.

Monitoring / telemetry:
- Metrics: stream_bytes_per_session, resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, duplicate_token_count.
- Logs: structured events for RESUME_REQUEST, RESUME_ACCEPTED, RESUME_REJECTED + opaque resume_token hashed for privacy.

Docs & examples to deliver:
- quickstart snippet (iterator and dispatcher patterns)
- migration guide from current async iterator helpers to ResumableStreamConsumer
- troubleshooting guide for resume failures and when to fall back to full re-run

Links / artifacts:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Python+Resumable+Stream+Consumer
- PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/2173
- Mock server test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/tree/main/tests/streaming/mock_server.py
- Related ticket: ENG-42100 (streaming iterator + checkpoint UX)

Open questions / trade-offs considered:
- Server-side resume tokens vs client-synthesized checkpoints: prefer server tokens when available, but synthesize checkpoints client-side when server doesn't provide them.
- Complexity: exposing both iterator and event-dispatcher to avoid forcing a single programming model. Keep iterator thin and composable.
- Persistence: whether to persist checkpoints to disk/DB for long-lived resumability. MVP will store in-memory and provide callbacks for apps to persist if needed.

Next steps:
- Spike: implement mock resume flow + unit tests (2 days) -> create PR -> internal review with SDK owners.
- After review: add docs + telemetry + enable feature flag for internal testers.
